## SimdVerlet.kt { #simdverlet-kt }

The particle solver: structure-of-arrays Verlet integration, directed distance constraints, and
the vector kernels that run both.

[`SimdVerlet`](simulation.md#simdverlet-kt-simdverlet) holds some thousands of particles in flat float arrays, pulls them toward each
other along up to four constraints each, and integrates them with Verlet. It is a CPU solver
with no renderer of its own and no geometry of its own: it deals in particle *indices*, and the
sibling files in this package are what turn those into things. [`Cloth`](simulation.md#cloth-kt-cloth) wires a rectangular grid
of constraints, [`Strand`](simulation.md#strand-kt-strand) a chain, [`Collider`](simulation.md#simdverletcolliders-kt-collider) the world to hit, [`Tearing`](simulation.md#simdverlettearing-kt-tearing) the edges that give
way, [`Wind`](simulation.md#simdverletwind-kt-wind) the air.

Three of its nested types carry the state:

- `State3` is structure-of-arrays: `x/y/z`, the previous positions `px/py/pz`, the force
  accumulators `ax/ay/az`, and an optional `invMass`. A particle is an index into all of those
  at once rather than an object, `invMass == 0` is how one is pinned, and the accumulators are
  scratch that [`step`](simulation.md#simdverlet-kt--simdverlet--step) zeroes at the top of every frame.
- `DirectedConstraints4` gives every particle four outgoing distance constraints: four neighbour
  indices, four rest lengths, four stiffnesses, in parallel arrays. Four is the
  up/down/left/right neighbourhood of an interior grid particle, so a cloth's whole topology
  fits with nothing spare. `DirectedConstraints3` is the same with three.
- `ConstraintScratch` is the gather buffer the 4-slot solve needs, one per worker thread.

*Directed* is literal. A constraint `i -> j` writes its correction only
to `i` and never scatters back to `j`, so disjoint particle ranges can be solved on separate
threads with a scratch each and the inner loop vectorises. The price is that a symmetric spring
is two constraints, and that it is possible to wire only one of them.

### The frame

[`step`](simulation.md#simdverlet-kt--simdverlet--step) runs, in this order: queued removals, zero the accumulators, gravity, the per-particle
force generators, the registered [`bulkForces`](simulation.md#simdverlet-kt--simdverlet--bulkforces), the caller's `accumulateForces`, `iterations`
passes of the constraint solve, Verlet integration, the registered [`positionProjections`](simulation.md#simdverlet-kt--simdverlet--positionprojections), and
the registered [`constraintEdits`](simulation.md#simdverlet-kt--simdverlet--constraintedits). Everything up to integration is force space; those last two
stages are the only places in a frame where positions are written directly.

Those three maps are how a layer in another file joins the frame without `step` knowing about
it: a whole-state force goes in `bulkForces`, a collider in `positionProjections`, tearing in
`constraintEdits`. Each is named and iterated in registration order, and each property's own
KDoc has why its stage sits where it does.

### The kernels

The companion carries the passes themselves as functions over arrays, each in a whole-state form
and a `...Range` form taking `start` and `endExclusive`: zeroing, Verlet integration, the 3- and
4-slot constraint solves, a velocity readback, and a spring toward a target point. The range
forms are what let `ForceExecutor` hand contiguous chunks to a fixed thread pool. That chunking
is coarse, two tasks per worker over a 256-particle minimum, because the target here is
thousands of particles rather than millions.

The solves and the bulk passes use the JDK Incubator Vector API, so a JVM that runs them needs
`--add-modules jdk.incubator.vector`. Field's own launches pass it already.

The number to know before tuning anything is the product `stiffness * iterations`. These are not
two independent knobs: the solve adds `iterations` corrections into the same accumulator with
nothing moving in between, so stiffness and iteration count multiply, and the product has a
ceiling past which an explicit integrator diverges.
`dev_docs/physics/SIMDVERLET_4_CONSTRAINTS.md` has the measurements.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/simulation/physics/SimdVerlet.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/simulation/physics/SimdVerlet/)

## SimdVerletColliders.kt { #simdverletcolliders-kt }

Collision shapes for [`SimdVerlet`](simulation.md#simdverlet-kt-simdverlet): the world layer of the particle solver.

A [`Collider`](simulation.md#simdverletcolliders-kt-collider) is a post-integration position projection registered through
[`SimdVerlet.addColliders`](simulation.md#simdverletcolliders-kt--addcolliders): no stiffness to tune, one square root per penetrating particle.
This file provides [`PlaneCollider`](simulation.md#simdverletcolliders-kt-planecollider), [`SphereCollider`](simulation.md#simdverletcolliders-kt-spherecollider), [`CapsuleCollider`](simulation.md#simdverletcolliders-kt-capsulecollider), [`BoxCollider`](simulation.md#simdverletcolliders-kt-boxcollider),
and [`SdfCollider`](simulation.md#simdverletcolliders-kt-sdfcollider) (for shapes expressed as a signed-distance function), plus [`ColliderSet`](simulation.md#simdverletcolliders-kt-colliderset),
which runs several colliders as one registered pass with optional multi-pass relaxation for
particles caught in a crease between two shapes.

The contact response applies Coulomb friction ([`Collider.friction`](simulation.md#simdverletcolliders-kt--collider--friction)), optional bounce
([`Collider.restitution`](simulation.md#simdverletcolliders-kt--collider--restitution)) and viscous tangential damping ([`Collider.tangentialDamping`](simulation.md#simdverletcolliders-kt--collider--tangentialdamping)).
Pinned particles (zero inverse mass) are never moved. [`PlaneCollider`](simulation.md#simdverletcolliders-kt-planecollider) and [`SphereCollider`](simulation.md#simdverletcolliders-kt-spherecollider)
carry a JDK Incubator Vector path alongside the scalar one; the rest are scalar.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/simulation/physics/SimdVerletColliders.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/simulation/physics/SimdVerletColliders/)

**Used in:** [Particles, welded, and traced](../chain_physics_render.md), [Physics: particles, constraints and cloth](../physics.md)

| <a id="simdverletcolliders-kt--collider--tangentialdamping"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tangentialDamping</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/simulation/physics/SimdVerletColliders/#L116) | Fraction of the *remaining* tangential velocity removed on every contact, unconditionally. The viscous companion to [`friction`](simulation.md#simdverletcolliders-kt--collider--friction), for a surface that should be sticky rather than merely rough. `0f` (the default) leaves Coulomb friction as the only tangential effect. |
| <a id="simdverletcolliders-kt--collider--restitution"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">restitution</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/simulation/physics/SimdVerletColliders/#L124) | Bounce: the fraction of an approaching normal velocity returned. `0f` is a dead surface, `1f` is lossless. A separating normal velocity is never touched, so this can only remove energy. Note that a high restitution never lets a particle come fully to rest — gravity re-penetrates by `g * dt^2` every frame and gets that fraction of it back. |
| <a id="simdverletcolliders-kt--collider--margin"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">margin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/simulation/physics/SimdVerletColliders/#L131) | Extra clearance held between a particle's centre and the surface — cloth half-thickness, or a particle radius. Positive values keep the sheet visibly off the shape, which is also what stops a wireframe from z-fighting the thing it is draped over. |
| <a id="simdverletcolliders-kt--collider--vectorized"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">vectorized</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/simulation/physics/SimdVerletColliders/#L134) | Use the vector path where there is one. `false` forces the scalar path; see the class KDoc. |
| <a id="simdverletcolliders-kt--collider--contacts"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">contacts</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/simulation/physics/SimdVerletColliders/#L142) | Number of particles the last `projectRange` found penetrating. Not a physical quantity — it is the "is this collider doing anything at all" readout, and what `SimdVerletCollidersTest` asserts a floor on so that a silently-missing contact fails loudly rather than passing as a cloth that happens to hang in the right place. |
| <a id="simdverletcolliders-kt--collider--projectrange"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">abstract</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">projectRange</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">state</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">SimdVerlet</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">State3</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">start</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">endExclusive</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/simulation/physics/SimdVerletColliders/#L151) | Projects the particles in `[start, endExclusive)` out of this shape and returns how many were penetrating. Writes `x/y/z` and `px/py/pz`; reads nothing else. Non-overlapping ranges touch disjoint particles, so this is range-parallel safe for one collider — several *colliders* over the same range are not, and [`ColliderSet`](simulation.md#simdverletcolliders-kt-colliderset) runs them in series. |
| <a id="simdverletcolliders-kt--collider--project"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">project</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">state</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">SimdVerlet</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">State3</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/simulation/physics/SimdVerletColliders/#L154) | `projectRange` over the whole active state. |
| <a id="simdverletcolliders-kt--collider--outline"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">abstract</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">outline</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">color</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec4</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">DEFAULT&#95;OUTLINE&#95;COLOR</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">thickness</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">1.6</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/simulation/physics/SimdVerletColliders/#L162) | The shape as `FLine`s, for drawing next to [`SimdVerlet.debugLines`](simulation.md#simdverletdebuglines-kt--debuglines). Not a renderer and not a mesh: a sphere is its silhouette circle in the XY plane, because the plane views these are for (`Box.showPlane`) project x/y and throw z away, and a great circle is the one curve that reads as "the thing the cloth is lying on" in that projection. |

## SimdVerletDebugLines.kt { #simdverletdebuglines-kt }

A [`SimdVerlet`](simulation.md#simdverlet-kt-simdverlet)'s particles and constraints as `FLine`s, for seeing what the solver holds rather
than what the scene means.

The file is one extension function, `debugLines`, and the list it returns is grouped by
appearance rather than by particle: at most four lines, in the order constraint edges, velocity
whiskers, unpinned particles, pinned particles, each already carrying its own colour and
thickness, and each left out when it would have been empty. So a caller restyles a whole
category by editing one element of that list, and the list's own length says only which
categories drew something.

## SimdVerletDyn4jBridge.kt { #simdverletdyn4jbridge-kt }

Runs a [`SimdVerlet`](simulation.md#simdverlet-kt-simdverlet) particle simulation and a [`Dyn4jScene`](simulation.md#dyn4jscene-kt-dyn4jscene) in one frame, so that chosen
particles collide with rigid bodies as circles while the rest stay ordinary particles.

The coupling is by nomination. [`nominate`](simulation.md#simdverletdyn4jbridge-kt--simdverletdyn4jbridge--nominate) takes a particle index and gives it a circle body in
the scene's dyn4j world; every other particle is untouched and costs nothing. Then each [`step`](simulation.md#simdverletdyn4jbridge-kt--simdverletdyn4jbridge--step)
advances the particle simulation, copies the nominated particles into their bodies, advances
dyn4j, and copies the bodies back. A nominated particle is still a Verlet particle that
constraints and force generators pull on; it spends the end of every frame being a rigid body
as well.

### The frame, and the SimdVerlet features it drops

[`step`](simulation.md#simdverletdyn4jbridge-kt--simdverletdyn4jbridge--step) does not call [`SimdVerlet.step`](simulation.md#simdverlet-kt--simdverlet--step). It runs its own copy of that frame, because it has to
decide per particle whether gravity applies. In order: queued removals, zero the accumulators,
gravity, the per-particle force generators, the constraint solve, Verlet integration, then the
dyn4j half.

What the copy leaves out is what this class does not support. There is no
[`SimdVerlet.bulkForces`](simulation.md#simdverlet-kt--simdverlet--bulkforces) pass, no `accumulateForces` hook, and neither post-integration stage
runs, so a `ColliderSet` in [`SimdVerlet.positionProjections`](simulation.md#simdverlet-kt--simdverlet--positionprojections) or a [`Tearing`](simulation.md#simdverlettearing-kt-tearing) in
[`SimdVerlet.constraintEdits`](simulation.md#simdverlet-kt--simdverlet--constraintedits) is silent under [`step`](simulation.md#simdverletdyn4jbridge-kt--simdverletdyn4jbridge--step). It also solves only
[`SimdVerlet.DirectedConstraints3`](simulation.md#simdverlet-kt--simdverlet--directedconstraints3), while [`Cloth`](simulation.md#cloth-kt-cloth) and [`Strand`](simulation.md#strand-kt-strand) build
[`SimdVerlet.DirectedConstraints4`](simulation.md#simdverlet-kt--simdverlet--directedconstraints4): step a cloth through this bridge and its constraints go
unsolved, because the default `constraints = sim.constraints` is null when the fabric is in
`constraints4`. So this is a bridge for loose particles rather than for fabric.

### Positions and velocities, both ways

A Verlet particle carries its velocity as the gap between `x` and `px`; a dyn4j body carries
one directly, in units per second. So the push sets the body to the particle's *previous*
position with `(x - px) / dt` as its velocity and lets dyn4j integrate that forward over the
same `dt`: the dyn4j step redoes the frame's last integration, this time with contacts in it.
The pull then writes `x` from the body's centre and rebuilds `px` as `centre - velocity * dt`,
so the particle's history after a frame comes from the body rather than surviving the hop.

Only `x`, `y`, `px` and `py` are written. [`CollisionPlane`](simulation.md#simdverletdyn4jbridge-kt-collisionplane) has one case and the constructor
requires it: this is the simulation's x/y plane, and `z` is left alone.

### Gravity, counted once

`DynGravityMode.MIRROR_SIM` copies [`step`](simulation.md#simdverletdyn4jbridge-kt--simdverletdyn4jbridge--step)'s `gravity` argument into the dyn4j world and
withholds it from the nominated particles in the Verlet pass, so dyn4j is the only thing
accelerating them. `DynGravityMode.ZERO` does the reverse: the dyn4j world gets none, and every
particle, nominated or not, gets the simulation's. Either way a particle falls once per frame.

The two are not the same fall. What the Verlet pass adds `gravity` to is the `ay` accumulator,
which is a *force* whenever the state has an `invMass` array, as `SimdVerlet.State3.empty`
allocates by default, so a heavy particle falls more slowly in the simulation. A dyn4j world
gravity is an acceleration, which every body there feels equally. They agree at inverse mass 1.

### Mass, radius, removal

Each frame the body's density is set so its mass is the particle's `1 / invMass` spread over
the circle's area, and an inverse mass of zero or less becomes `MassType.INFINITE`, the same
convention that pins a particle in the solver. That conversion is cached and redone only when
the particle's inverse mass changes.

Changing [`BulletSpec.radius`](simulation.md#simdverletdyn4jbridge-kt--bulletspec--radius) destroys the body and builds a new one, at the next [`step`](simulation.md#simdverletdyn4jbridge-kt--simdverletdyn4jbridge--step) rather
than when the spec changes, because the fixture's circle is not resized in place. Friction and
restitution are written to the existing fixture instead. [`unnominate`](simulation.md#simdverletdyn4jbridge-kt--simdverletdyn4jbridge--unnominate) and [`clearNominations`](simulation.md#simdverletdyn4jbridge-kt--simdverletdyn4jbridge--clearnominations)
take the bodies back out of the world.

Nominations are keyed by particle index, and `SimdVerlet`'s removal is a swap compaction: a
deleted slot is filled from the tail. Each frame drops the nominations whose index has fallen
out of range, which is as much as an index can tell it — a nomination whose index survives a
removal now names whichever particle was swapped into that slot. Re-nominate after removing
particles.

Nothing in the repository constructs one of these and no test covers it. It is a surface for
box code to call, and there is no 3D equivalent: [`JoltPhysicsWorld`](simulation.md#joltphysicsworld-kt-joltphysicsworld) is a rigid-body world of
its own, with nothing wiring it to a particle simulation.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/simulation/physics/SimdVerletDyn4jBridge.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/simulation/physics/SimdVerletDyn4jBridge/)

## SimdVerletTearing.kt { #simdverlettearing-kt }

Tearing for [`SimdVerlet`](simulation.md#simdverlet-kt-simdverlet): retiring over-stretched distance constraints, and the two measurements
that say where to set the threshold.

[`Tearing`](simulation.md#simdverlettearing-kt-tearing) retires a constraint once it has been stretched past a fraction of its rest length, so
a sheet under load rips instead of stretching forever. It runs as a constraint-edit pass,
registered by [`SimdVerlet.addTearing`](simulation.md#simdverlettearing-kt--addtearing) on a bare simulation or by [`Cloth.enableTearing`](simulation.md#simdverlettearing-kt--enabletearing) on a
[`Cloth`](simulation.md#cloth-kt-cloth). Both hand back the live object, so a threshold can be retuned or an edge cut by hand
between frames, and the cloth version additionally drops the curvature stencil at each lip of a
tear, without which the curvature force goes on flattening the sheet across a rip the solver has
already made.

Strain is `(distance - rest) / rest` throughout, so a threshold is a fraction rather than a
length, and it can be read off a measurement instead of found by bisection.
[`SimdVerlet.peakStrain`](simulation.md#simdverlettearing-kt--peakstrain) is that measurement over a whole simulation: a threshold below the strain
a sheet settles at tears it while it hangs at rest. [`SimdVerlet.liveEdgeCount`](simulation.md#simdverlettearing-kt--liveedgecount) counts surviving
edges the way the debug drawing does, a symmetric pair counted once, so a line lost from the
picture and an edge torn in the solver are the same number.

## SimdVerletWind.kt { #simdverletwind-kt }

Wind for [`SimdVerlet`](simulation.md#simdverlet-kt-simdverlet): per-particle drag, per-quad cloth aerodynamics, and the reproducible
gust field both of them sample.

The two force models answer different questions, and a sheet that is meant to flutter rather
than lean needs the second one.

**Per-particle drag** ([`SimdVerlet.addWind`](simulation.md#simdverletwind-kt--addwind)) is `F = drag * (w - v)` per particle, where `w` is
the wind velocity at that point and `v = (x - px) / dt` is the Verlet velocity. It applies to
anything made of particles (a rope, a point cloud, a cloth), and it cannot see which way fabric
is facing, because a particle has no orientation: a sheet edge-on to the wind is pushed exactly
as hard as a sheet face-on, and under a steady wind such a cloth reaches an equilibrium lean and
stays there.

**Per-quad aerodynamics** ([`Cloth.addWind`](simulation.md#simdverletwind-kt--addwind)) reads the sheet's own topology, which costs nothing:
a [`Cloth`](simulation.md#cloth-kt-cloth) is a contiguous row-major grid, so the quad at `(col, row)` is four adds. For each quad
it takes the normal from the diagonals, the area from half that normal's length, the relative
velocity from the mean of the four corners, and applies

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
F = 0.5 * rho * Cd * A * (n . v_rel) * |n . v_rel| * n
```

quartered onto the corners, plus an optional tangential term. Flutter comes out of the signed
`n . v_rel` factor: a quad turning edge-on stops being pushed, overshoots, catches the wind on
its other face, and the instability travels down the sheet as a wave.

`SimdVerletWindTest` measures both models through the same measurement. Two identical 12 x 12
sheets at rest in the same wind, one face-on and one edge-on, differ by more than twenty times
in the force the per-quad pass puts into them, and what little the edge-on sheet gets is all
skin friction: set `ClothWind.tangentialCoefficient` to zero and its normal force drops below a
millionth of the face-on total. The drag pass gives the two sheets the same force to within a
part in 100000, because a particle has no orientation to have.

The other measurement is sustained motion: a 20 x 12 flag in an 8-unit wind with 60 % gusts,
scored as trailing-edge travel per frame once the transient has passed, with the per-quad pass
on and off. What the test asserts is the shape rather than the figures. Per-quad always adds
motion; it adds more than 2.5 times as much at `Wind.drag = 0.05`, and less than 1.5 times as
much by `0.5`. So the advantage is a low-drag one. Turn drag up and the drag pass is doing the
forcing, and the sheet is being carried rather than flying.

### The gust field

`Wind.turbulence` adds gusts on top of the mean `Wind.velocityX`/`velocityY`/`velocityZ`. The
field is a small closed-form spectrum: a few sines per axis, with directions, spatial
frequencies, temporal frequencies and phases all derived from the seed. It is not a noise
lattice and not a fluid simulation, because what it has to be is reproducible and grid-free.
Two runs at the same seed produce the same sheet, so a test can assert something about it and a
capture can be re-taken; and a lattice can align its cells with the cloth's own grid spacing and
stand a pattern in the sheet. A sum of sines has no lattice to align, and costs three sines per
octave per sample.

Gust amplitude is `turbulence` times the mean wind's speed, so `turbulence = 0.4f` is gusts of
about 40 % whatever the wind is set to, and `0f` is a steady stream.

### Wind time

`Wind.time` advances by `dt` on every pass, so a registered wind is a running one. Set it to
drive the gusts from somewhere else (a transport, a scrub bar); reset it to zero to replay a
gust exactly.

## Strand.kt { #strand-kt }

A rope inside somebody else's [`SimdVerlet`](simulation.md#simdverlet-kt-simdverlet): the one-dimensional sibling of [`Cloth`](simulation.md#cloth-kt-cloth), and the same
shape of thing. `sim.addStrand(...)` (or `Strand.addTo`) appends `count` particles to a
simulation that may already contain others, chains them through a
[`SimdVerlet.DirectedConstraints4`](simulation.md#simdverlet-kt--simdverlet--directedconstraints4), and hands back a handle that speaks node indices.

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
val sim = SimdVerlet(SimdVerlet.State3.empty())
val rope = sim.addStrand(count = 40, spacing = 0.12f, stiffness = 60f)
rope.pin(0)
while (true) { rope.step(gravity = 9.8f, iterations = 16); draw(rope.lines()) }
```

### Why every node has two spare slots

A chain node spends slot 0 on its successor and slot 1 on its predecessor; the ends use one
each. That leaves **slots 2 and 3 free on every node of every rope**, which is what
`Strand.attachTo` spends. A rope can be tied to a cloth corner, to another rope, or to any
particle in the simulation with a spare slot, and the join is an ordinary symmetric distance
constraint that the same solver, the same colliders and the same [`Tearing`](simulation.md#simdverlettearing-kt-tearing) already understand.
So a tied rope tears at its knot under enough load.

What it cannot tie to is a cloth's *interior*, which has all four slots on its axis neighbours.
`attachTo` throws there and names the particle index rather than ignoring the tie. Corners have
two free slots and edges have one.

### Bending

`Strand.bendStiffness` straightens the rope by moving each interior node toward the midpoint of
its two neighbours: the 1-D case of [`Cloth`](simulation.md#cloth-kt-cloth)'s curvature idea, but as a **position projection**
in `SimdVerlet.positionProjections` rather than a force.

A projection rather than a force, because a curvature force would sit on the solver's
`stiffness * iterations` scale, where the product has a divergence ceiling in `dt`, and the
strength that holds a rope straight is above it: turned up far enough such a force thrashes
instead of stiffening. A projection has no stiffness, so it has no ceiling. The projection
itself is the standard mass-weighted one — `C = b - (a+c)/2`, corrections `Δb = +w_b·d/S`,
`Δa = Δc = -w·d/2S` with `S = w_b + (w_a + w_c)/4` — applied to `x` *and* `px` together so it
injects no velocity and can add no energy, and swept in **three colours** so that overlapping
stencils do not stack their corrections on top of each other. `bendStiffness` is clamped to
`0..1`, and `Strand.MAX_BEND_CORRECTION` is what `1` maps onto: the stiffest correction this
integrator holds, rather than a full one.

What it controls is **how tightly the rope can fold**, which is not the same thing as how stiff
the rope is. `StrandTest` heaps a 50-node rope on a floor between two anchors and reads the mean
joint angle: it falls with every increase in `bendStiffness`, and by `1.0` it is under a third of
the limp rope's, with no sharp corner left.

On a *cantilever* it does almost nothing, because a rope hanging under gravity is already
straight and the base moment a cantilever needs is not something a local three-node stencil can
supply. For a rod, add distance constraints across the gaps rather than turning this up.

`0f` is the default: a rope is limp unless told otherwise.

One ordering caveat. Projections run in registration order, so a strand created *before* its
colliders bends first and is then pushed out of the world. Create the strand after the colliders
and the last word belongs to bending, and a stiff rope can end a frame slightly inside a shape.

### Stability

The same contract as [`Cloth`](simulation.md#cloth-kt-cloth): the rope's particles are the contiguous range
`[base, base + count)`, so it does not survive particle removal anywhere below its own top
index. Appending after it is fine.

`Strand.step`, `Strand.lines` and the mutators serialize on this strand's own monitor.

## FastMechanics.kt { #fastmechanics-kt }

The packed kernel for the membrane energy: [`FastMechanics`](simulation.md#fastmechanics-kt-fastmechanics) computes the same energy and gradient
as [`Mechanics`](simulation.md#mechanics-kt-mechanics) from flat arrays prepacked once per solve.

[`InflationSolver`](simulation.md#solver-kt-inflationsolver) builds one when [`SolveOptions`](simulation.md#solver-kt-solveoptions) has `fastKernel` set and minimises against it,
then re-evaluates each step through [`Mechanics`](simulation.md#mechanics-kt-mechanics), so every residual and per-step figure it
reports comes from the reference kernel. The [`Evaluation`](simulation.md#mechanics-kt-evaluation) returned here carries no [`FilmState`](simulation.md#mechanics-kt-filmstate)
or [`TapeState`](simulation.md#mechanics-kt-tapestate); per-triangle and per-tape detail exists only on the reference path.
`PressureTest.materialBranchesForcesAndPackedKernelAgree` holds the two kernels to 1e-7 on
energy and on every gradient component, across both gas modes and three deformations.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/simulation/physics/pressure/FastMechanics.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/simulation/physics/pressure/FastMechanics/)

## Mechanics.kt { #mechanics-kt }

The membrane energy and its gradient: [`Mechanics`](simulation.md#mechanics-kt-mechanics) evaluates film, tape, tether, gravity, ground
contact and gas work for one set of node positions under a [`LoadCase`](simulation.md#mechanics-kt-loadcase).

Gas is either held at a regulated pressure or sealed and isothermal ([`GasMode`](simulation.md#mechanics-kt-gasmode)). The
[`Evaluation`](simulation.md#mechanics-kt-evaluation) it returns carries per-triangle [`FilmState`](simulation.md#mechanics-kt-filmstate) and per-tape [`TapeState`](simulation.md#mechanics-kt-tapestate) alongside the
energy, which [`InflationSolver`](simulation.md#solver-kt-inflationsolver) minimises.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/simulation/physics/pressure/Mechanics.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/simulation/physics/pressure/Mechanics/)

**Used in:** [Pressure membranes](../pressure_membranes.md)

Total-Lagrangian constant-strain triangles; large rotations, elastic Green strain. Isotropic plane-stress St Venant--Kirchhoff energy relaxed in compressive principal directions (taut / uniaxially wrinkled / slack). No bending or wrinkle wavelength. Film force resultants are pushed into the current surface, in N per current metre. This elastic law does not model bending, self-contact, plasticity or material failure.

## MinimumSearch.kt { #minimumsearch-kt }

A sampled check of whether a solved membrane sits at an energy minimum: [`MinimumSearch`](simulation.md#minimumsearch-kt-minimumsearch) estimates
the lowest curvature with a finite-difference Lanczos iteration and tries displacements along it and along eight smoothed random directions.

The result is a [`MinimumAudit`](simulation.md#minimumsearch-kt-minimumaudit), which also folds in a [`ShapeAudit`](simulation.md#shapeaudit-kt-shapeaudit) of the deformed skin. A
positive Ritz value is not a stability certificate; the audit reports whether a lower-energy
direction was found in the directions it sampled.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/simulation/physics/pressure/MinimumSearch.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/simulation/physics/pressure/MinimumSearch/)

## Model.kt { #model-kt }

The input model for the pressure-membrane solver: a closed triangulated [`Envelope`](simulation.md#model-kt-envelope) whose
triangles each carry a [`Film`](simulation.md#model-kt-film), with [`Tape`](simulation.md#model-kt-tape) reinforcements, [`Tether`](simulation.md#model-kt-tether) and [`Anchor`](simulation.md#model-kt-anchor) supports, all in SI units.

Positions are a flat `DoubleArray` of x, y, z per node, read with [`point`](simulation.md#model-kt--point). [`SurfacePoint`](simulation.md#model-kt-surfacepoint)
attaches a tape or tether to fixed barycentric weights on the material, so an attachment moves
with the deformed skin. [`volume`](simulation.md#model-kt--volume) gives the enclosed volume that the gas load acts on.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/simulation/physics/pressure/Model.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/simulation/physics/pressure/Model/)

## NewtonPolish.kt { #newtonpolish-kt }

The optional Newton step that finishes an inflation solve: [`NewtonPolish`](simulation.md#newtonpolish-kt-newtonpolish) takes the positions
L-BFGS reached and drives the free-node force residual down further.

[`InflationSolver`](simulation.md#solver-kt-inflationsolver) runs it once per pressure step, and only when that residual sits above the
step's acceptance gate but close to it. Curvature enters as Hessian-vector products built from
central differences of the gradient, two energy evaluations each, so no Hessian is ever
assembled. The conjugate-gradient inner solve is preconditioned by the energy diagonal from
[`MinimumSearch`](simulation.md#minimumsearch-kt-minimumsearch) and truncated at the trust-region boundary or on negative curvature, and anchors
with no stiffness stay out of the free set. [`SolveOptions`](simulation.md#solver-kt-solveoptions) carries the flag that turns it off.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/simulation/physics/pressure/NewtonPolish.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/simulation/physics/pressure/NewtonPolish/)

## ShapeAudit.kt { #shapeaudit-kt }

Geometric checks on a deformed pressure envelope: [`ShapeAudits`](simulation.md#shapeaudit-kt-shapeaudits) finds triangle self-intersections,
sharp folds between neighbouring triangles, panel seams and multi-panel junction angles.

The checks read the computed triangles only, independent of how a viewer shades or explodes them.

## Solver.kt { #solver-kt }

[`InflationSolver`](simulation.md#solver-kt-inflationsolver) relaxes an [`Envelope`](simulation.md#model-kt-envelope) to equilibrium by raising pressure in steps and
minimising the [`Mechanics`](simulation.md#mechanics-kt-mechanics) energy at each one with Field's L-BFGS.

A step is accepted on free-force residuals in newtons, not on optimiser step size, and the
[`Solution`](simulation.md#solver-kt-solution) reports anchor reactions, force and moment balance and the step `Solution.history`.
A failed continuation returns unconverged at the load fraction it reached. [`SolveOptions`](simulation.md#solver-kt-solveoptions)
sets the step count, tolerances and the optional Newton polish.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/simulation/physics/pressure/Solver.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/simulation/physics/pressure/Solver/)

Acceptance uses free-force residuals in N, not optimizer step size. Failed continuation returns an unconverged result with its actual load fraction in `Solution.history`. Cancellation propagates. A converged force balance is not proof of a minimum; [`MinimumSearch`](simulation.md#minimumsearch-kt-minimumsearch) offers a sampled diagnostic. |
